title: The settings window: Computers, What Ember did, Commands, accessibility
owns: the settings sections of app/renderer/home/** (computers*.ts, copy.ts, styles.css, index.html), app/main/doctor.ts check names

findings.title: “What Ember did” shows nothing for commands, SSH connections or WSL, and those entries crowd out the real ones
findings.scenario: A user turns on commands for build-01 and asks Ember to clean the build folder. Ember asks, the user allows, the command runs. Settings › What Ember did lists only the Task line and 'Finished'. It does not show the command, the question that was answered, a refused command, or an SSH or WSL connection event. docs/DEVELOPING.md:140 promises the list shows 'every request, question, action and refusal'. Each command also writes about 3 to 5 audit lines (decided, answered, started, ended). `activity()` returns only the newest 150 audit entries and the page hides the non-displayable ones, so after roughly 30 to 50 commands the timeline can fall back to 'Nothing yet. When Ember works in your apps…' while the audit log is busy.
findings.evidence: describeEntry() has no case for event 'command' | 'remote' | 'wsl' and returns null (copy.ts:216-218), although audit.ts:15 defines those events and commands/flow.ts:542-556, 654, 804, 826 and 963 write them. I ran describeEntry on real-shaped entries: command/decided, answered and ended, remote/failed and wsl/started all returned null, while an action entry returned a row. main.ts:375 returns `audit.recent(150)` unfiltered (audit.ts:43).
findings.fix: Add rows for command events, for example tag 'Command' and what 'Run `rm -rf build` on build-01', with 'You allowed' / 'You said no' / 'Refused' from the decided and answered phases and 'Didn't work' on a non-zero end, plus rows for connection events. Also filter `recent()` to displayable events before slicing, or request more than 150.

findings.title: [hidden] is overridden by display rules: the SSH add form shows under an SSH-off policy, and the Computers and Commands shells show when no targets runtime answers
findings.scenario: (1) An organisation sets features.ssh:false. computers.ts sets #host-form.hidden=true, but `.add-row{display:flex}` wins over the UA hidden rule, so the Settings window still shows 'An SSH host, e.g. build-01…' with a working-looking Connect button beside 'Your organisation doesn't allow Ember on other computers.' (2) If the targets list never resolves (the code comment says the sections 'stay hidden'), `section{display:grid}` (styles.css:20) shows empty Computers and Commands shells (headings, intro text, 'Open the command window') while their sidebar links stay hidden.
findings.evidence: Probe of computed styles: #host-form hidden=true display=flex (managed scenario). #computers and #commands hidden=true display=grid with no emberTargets. Screenshot of case 1: managed-dark-full-t2.png.
findings.fix: Add `section[hidden], .add-row[hidden] { display: none; }`, or a global `[hidden]{display:none !important}` in ember.css.

findings.title: Setup-check fix buttons: identical names, silent failure, focus lost
findings.scenario: (a) On macOS up to four buttons all read 'Open System Settings'. On Windows each WSL distro gets its own 'Turn on'. A screen reader user browsing buttons cannot tell which row each belongs to. (b) When a fix is refused, the page writes 'Couldn't change it: …' into the row's detail span. That span is not a live region, and focus has already dropped to the body, so nothing is announced and the user is left on the page body with no feedback.
findings.evidence: Accessibility tree dump aria-win.txt shows two 'button "Turn on"'. Probe with a refused fix: activeElement became BODY, detail text changed, and no [aria-live]/[role=status|alert] ancestor exists.
findings.fix: Set btn aria-label to `${c.label}: ${fixLabel}` (for example 'Accessibility in Ubuntu: Turn on'). Put the failure message in a role=status element, and on failure re-enable the button and refocus it instead of leaving focus on the body.

findings.title: SSH rows say “Connected: nothing yet”, “Connected: isn't answering” and “commands once you agree only”
findings.scenario: A user adds a headless server. Commands are off by default, so the row reads 'Connected: nothing yet', with no pointer to the Commands switch below. A stalled link shows 'Connected: isn't answering', which contradicts itself. A host waiting for a newer consent card shows 'Connected: commands once you agree only'.
findings.evidence: sshStatus() prefixes 'Connected: ' to registry.ts canWords(), which returns 'nothing yet', 'isn't answering', or `${c} only` with c='commands once you agree' (registry.ts:109-117, 181-194). I built the registry for those link states: the row statuses were exactly those three strings.
findings.fix: Map the SSH status from state and capability in the settings copy rather than echoing `can`. For example 'Connected. Turn on commands below to use it', 'Connected, but not answering', 'Connected. Commands once you agree'. Fix canWords' `commands once you agree only`.

findings.title: Every “Ask me before every command” switch has the same accessible name
findings.scenario: With commands on for this computer and an SSH host or a WSL distro, a screen reader user listing form controls hears 'Ask me before every command' two or three times, with no hint which computer each one belongs to. The switches are plain labels in a div, not grouped.
findings.evidence: Accessibility tree dump aria-win.txt shows 'switch "Ask me before every command"' repeated after each 'Run commands …' switch (the label constant comes from ASK_EVERY_SWITCH, computers-copy.ts:21).
findings.fix: Give each sub-switch an aria-label such as 'Ask me before every command on build-01', or name the group with role=group and aria-labelledby the parent switch's label.

findings.title: The SSH host field is cleared before the connection result is known
findings.scenario: A user types a slightly wrong host and presses Connect. The field empties at once, and the failure ('That isn't an SSH host Ember can use…' or a connection error) appears in a message at the bottom of the section. They have to retype the whole host to fix a typo. The never-look form clears only after success, so the two forms behave differently.
findings.evidence: Code: `input.value = ""; void act({ kind: "add", dest }, …)`. The result arrives from api.act() later and never restores the value.
findings.fix: Clear the field only when the act returns ok, or restore the typed value on a failure.

findings.title: Sidebar labels differ from the section headings they open
findings.scenario: The sidebar says 'Privacy', 'Comfort', 'Activity' and 'Setup', but the headings (and docs/DEVELOPING.md) say 'Apps & privacy', 'Comfort & access', 'What Ember did' and 'Setup check'. A screen reader user who activates 'Activity' lands on 'What Ember did'.
findings.evidence: index.html:22 versus :106, :154, :176, :184. Screenshot linux-main-dark.png.
findings.fix: Use the heading text in the sidebar (or shorten both), for example 'Apps & privacy' and 'What Ember did'.

findings.title: Computers rows are cramped at the default window size, and “Forget” has no confirmation beside Disconnect
findings.scenario: At the default 760 px window the content column is about 500 px. The actions block takes up to 60% of the row, so 'build-01 · deploy@build-01.example.com' breaks mid-address and 'Connected: apps and commands' wraps. The three red-text buttons wrap onto two lines, with 'Remove Ember from build-01' under Disconnect and Forget. Forget (which drops the host record and its consent) is one click from Disconnect with no confirmation, while the less drastic Remove has one. At 420 px the host placeholder is cut off at 'deploy@bu'.
findings.evidence: Screenshots linux-main-dark-full-t2.png, narrow-dark-full-t3.png, wm-open-t2.png (very long host name case).
findings.fix: Stack the row (name and status on top, actions below), shorten the third button to 'Remove helper', ask before Forget or make it less prominent, and shorten the placeholder.

findings.title: Small copy slips in the welcome text and labels
findings.scenario: 'Windows on your never-look list' reads as the operating system on a Windows PC. The 'Other computers and commands' line (index.html:36) tells Linux and macOS users that Ember works in WSL. 'Offer to bring Ember along when I connect with ssh' writes SSH in lower case, unlike every other label. 'Model for tasks (needs vision)' uses jargon. The sign-in row wraps with a dangling '—' at the start of a line ('— enter it at github.com/login/device'). The Linux friendly-name table lacks common apps, so grants read 'Google-chrome' or 'Code'.
findings.evidence: index.html:31, 36, 73; computers-copy.ts:18; main.ts:554; shared/apps.ts:20-43 and capitalised() at :100. Screenshots signin-code.png and stress-full-t1.png.
findings.fix: Say 'App windows on your never-look list', show the WSL part only on Windows, write 'SSH', say 'must be able to read images', put the dash inside a nowrap span or drop it, and add google-chrome, code and slack to the Linux name table.

findings.title: Setup-check fix buttons all have the same name ('Turn on', 'Open System Settings'), unlike every other list button
findings.scenario: On macOS a VoiceOver user setting up permissions Tabs to four identical 'Open System Settings' buttons (Accessibility, Screen Recording, Input Monitoring, Microphone) and hears no indication which pane each opens. On Linux and Windows several 'Turn on' buttons are the same. The rows' computers, grants and never-look buttons already carry specific aria-labels.
findings.evidence: AX tree of the settings window with two failing checks: `button 'Turn on'` twice with listitem names empty (home.mjs). Code: `btn.textContent = platform?.fixLabels[fix] ?? 'Turn on'` and no aria-label or aria-describedby.
findings.fix: Set btn.setAttribute('aria-label', `${label text}: ${c.label}`) or aria-describedby on the row's label span, so the name reads 'Open System Settings: Screen Recording'.

findings.title: First-run: focus is dropped to <body> when Start Ember removes its own button
findings.scenario: A keyboard or screen-reader user ticks 'I agree' and presses Start Ember. The page then hides the start row (and the Start button that holds focus) and reveals all the after-setup sections. Focus falls to the document body, and nothing announces that setup finished or where they are. The tagline is the only live text.
findings.evidence: Chromium run (home-focus.mjs): focus on #start, Enter, then the settings echo with onboarded:true. document.activeElement === BODY and start-row hidden=true. $('start').addEventListener('click') (line 150) only calls updateSettings. By contrast renderAgent hands focus on when its buttons disappear.
findings.fix: When onboarded flips to true while Start (or #agree) has focus, move focus to the 'Your Ember' heading (like showSection) or to the tagline region, and put 'Ember has started' in the status line.

findings.title: Settings: the Size slider's <output> is an implicit live region, so each arrow key speaks the new value twice
findings.scenario: A screen-reader user changes the character size with the arrow keys. The slider's aria-valuetext announces '62 pixels' and the <output id='size-out'> (role status, live polite) also announces '62 px'.
findings.evidence: AX tree (home.mjs): `slider 'Size '` with `LabelText > status '' live='polite'`. `<label for='size'>Size <output id='size-out' for='size'>…</output></label>`.
findings.fix: Add role='presentation' aria-live='off' to the output (or make it a plain <span aria-hidden='true'>) and keep aria-valuetext as the one source.

findings.title: Add-computer form empties the field before the result and gives no feedback while the card or connection is pending
findings.scenario: The user types 'bild-01.example.com' and presses Connect. The field clears at once. Ember answers 'Ember can't find bild-01.example.com. Check the name, or add it to your SSH config.' and the user must retype the whole name to fix a typo. Meanwhile (the SSH card waiting, or a 30 s connect) the page shows nothing; no row exists until the host is saved after the card.
findings.evidence: Playwright harness: right after Enter the input value was '' and the act was pending; after the act resolved {ok:false} the input stayed '' and the message showed. computers.ts clears the input before awaiting act().
findings.fix: Clear the field only on success, and show 'Waiting for your OK in the window that opened…' / 'Connecting…' in the message line while the act is pending.

findings.title: Status words in Settings' Computers list mislead: 'Connected: nothing yet', 'Connected: isn't answering', WSL distros 'Not available' when only WSL is off, 'Disconnect' while connecting
findings.scenario: A connected headless host with commands off reads 'Connected: nothing yet', with no hint that turning commands on is the next step. A stalled link reads 'Connected: isn't answering'. With WSL off every distro reads 'Not available' (note: 'WSL is off in Ember') although the distro is fine and one switch away. A row that is still connecting offers 'Disconnect' where 'Cancel' is meant.
findings.evidence: Rendered the Computers section with summaries can 'nothing yet' and 'isn't answering' and WSL 'unavailable' rows: the strings above appear. sshStatus() builds 'Connected: ${t.can}', wslStatus() maps unavailable to 'Not available', and connected includes state 'connecting'.
findings.fix: 'Connected, commands off' (with a hint or link to the Commands switch), 'Connected, not answering', 'Off' for WSL-disabled distros, and 'Cancel' while connecting.

findings.title: 'Remove Ember from <computer>' gives no progress, no cancel and no success message, and silently forgets the computer
findings.scenario: The user confirms the dialog. Ember connects (possibly with a password or host-key card that is titled only 'Sign in to build-01', with no mention of removal) and runs the removal, which can take a minute. The row shows no change. If a task or command is running there it is stopped with no warning in the dialog. On success the row vanishes with no message, and the host record and its commands consent are also deleted (so the commands and SSH cards must be accepted again on re-adding). The dialog doesn't say any of that.
findings.evidence: runtime.ts:837 'uninstall' awaits connections.uninstall(host) then forget(host.id), with no bubble or message. The progress handler ignores steps unless state is 'connecting'. The confirm text is: 'Remove Ember's helper from build-01? Its record of what Ember did there stays on build-01.'
findings.fix: Show 'Removing Ember from build-01…' with a Cancel in the row, say 'Removed. build-01 is no longer in your list' on success, and add 'It also stops anything running there and forgets the computer here' to the confirm.

findings.title: Remote app grants are listed in Settings as raw keys ('ssh:build-01:gedit', 'Remove ssh:build-01:gedit')
findings.area: Settings: apps Ember may act in / WSL and SSH apps
findings.scenario: The user answers 'Always in gedit' for a task on build-01. Under 'Apps Ember may act in without asking first' the entry reads 'ssh:build-01:gedit', and its Remove button's accessible name is 'Remove ssh:build-01:gedit'. Local entries read 'gedit'.
findings.evidence: friendlyApp('ssh:build-01:gedit') returned 'ssh:build-01:gedit' unchanged (run with esbuild); worker.ts stores grants under hands.grantKey, which is `${id}:${app}` for remote targets.
findings.fix: Render 'gedit on build-01' (and 'gedit in Ubuntu (WSL)') for keys with an 'ssh:<id>:' prefix.

findings.title: Small copy and layout issues in Settings › Computers
findings.scenario: The intro says 'Ember can work… in WSL' on Linux and macOS, where WSL is never offered. The host field's placeholder is cut at narrow widths ('…deploy@bu'). The 'Let Ember work in WSL' switch sits below every SSH row, so a Windows user with several computers has to scroll for it. Nothing shows which distro 'WSL' and 'Linux' mean (the default one), so with two distros the user can't tell where 'in WSL' goes.
findings.evidence: Rendered at 900 and 420 px (Linux, then Windows with WSL rows): intro text above, placeholder truncated at 420 px, the switch after the rows. The summary never marks the default distro.
findings.fix: Show the WSL sentence only on Windows. Shorten the placeholder ('build-01 or user@host'). Put the WSL switch above the list and mark the default distro 'Default for "in WSL"'.

findings.title: "What Ember did" shows lowercase, third-person and model-facing fragments as the reason
findings.scenario: The user opens What Ember did. Refusal and failure reasons are raw audit text: "this app is on the user's never-look list", "it didn't turn on", "no window known yet", "the control a click goes to can't be found" (all lowercase), and "The user moved the mouse or pressed a key, so Ember let go." (the user is called "the user"). The same list mixes capitalised and lowercase reasons, and the user is sometimes "the user" and sometimes "your" ("your organisation has turned off Ember acting in apps").
findings.evidence: Rendered audit entries through the real settings window (shots/activity.png and the dumped text): lines "this app is on the user's never-look list", "first action in …", "your organisation has turned off Ember acting in apps", "The user moved the mouse or pressed a key, so Ember let go.", "it didn't turn on", "no window known yet". describeEntry passes e.reason straight through (copy.ts:209), and forUser strips only the listed tool names and codes. Sources: policy.ts:2018-2024, borrow.ts:29, worker.ts:1915 and the many lowercase reasons at policy.ts:1486-1962.
findings.fix: Normalise in describeEntry: capitalise the first letter, end with a full stop, map "the user's" to "your" and "The user" to "You" (e.g. "This app is on your never-look list.", "You moved the mouse or pressed a key, so Ember let go."). Better, store a short user wording beside the model wording in the audit entry.

findings.title: "What Ember did" omits commands, connections and WSL entries, though the docs say it lists every action
findings.scenario: The user turns on Commands, a task runs `npm test` on build-01 and a dangerous command is allowed or refused. Settings › What Ember did shows only the task's "Task" and "Finished" lines. No line says which command ran, where, whether it asked or was allowed, or that an SSH connection was made. docs/DEVELOPING.md:140 says the list "lists every request, question, action and refusal", and the welcome page promises "a record of every action it took".
findings.evidence: Called describeEntry with audit entries {event:"command",phase:"decision"|"started"|"ended"}, {event:"remote"} and {event:"wsl"}: all return null (probe4). The switch handles only task, decision, confirm, action and stop (copy.ts:196-218) and the default returns null; flow.ts:542, 804 and 827 audit with event "command".
findings.fix: Add cases for command ("Ran" / "Asked you" / "Refused" with the target, shell and exit status, never the command text) and for remote or WSL connects and disconnects, or change the docs and the fold hint to say commands and connections are only in the audit folder.

findings.title: The same check has different names in the settings window and in `ember doctor`
findings.scenario: On Linux the settings window calls the accessibility row "Screen reading" while `ember doctor` calls it "Reading apps" (docs/DEVELOPING.md refers to "Screen reading"). On macOS the window says "Reading and using apps", "Applications folder" and "Microphone", while the CLI says "Accessibility", "Location" and "Microphone access", and README calls the permission "Accessibility". The tool is "check-up" in the CLI heading, "Setup check" in the window and "doctor" in the command.
findings.evidence: Ran `electron . --doctor`: "warn  Reading apps  Python accessibility bindings are missing."; the settings window dump: "Screen reading — Python accessibility bindings are missing: sudo dnf install python3-pyatspi". Sources: doctor.ts:141, environment.ts:174-178, 270-271, 291, darwin/system/doctor.ts:20-45.
findings.fix: Use one label per check in both surfaces (e.g. "Reading apps") and one name for the tool ("setup check") in the README, window and CLI heading.

findings.title: Settings sidebar is cut off at the window's minimum height with no visible scrollbar
findings.scenario: The sidebar is fixed, overflow:auto and scrollbar-width:none (the horizontal pill row's setting is inherited by the vertical sidebar too). With Computers and Commands shown it has 11 links and needs 438 px, but the window may be as short as 420 px (windows.ts minHeight:420). 'About' (and part of 'Setup') sit past the bottom and the only way to reach them is the mouse wheel or Tab, with nothing hinting that the list scrolls.
findings.evidence: Rendered home at 760x420 with the targets runtime present: #jump scrollHeight 438 vs clientHeight 420, overflowY auto, scrollbar-width none (sidebar.mjs, shots/home-minheight.png).
findings.fix: Raise the home window's minHeight to at least 480, or remove scrollbar-width:none from the wide-sidebar rule so the slim ember.css scrollbar shows (keep it only for the narrow horizontal row).
